thesis: A wide-moat platform with flat 32.2% operating margin trades below its 5y minimum earnings multiples and below even its mechanical bear fair value, where the price assumes the AI capex surge never converts back to cash.
reason: The fall is a capex-driven FCF reset and chip-curb sentiment, not a break in the core franchise: margins and returns hold, the balance sheet funds the spend. Scorecard conviction 4 despite a high key risk; Python sizes it. China/HK cap and cash floor require a replacement.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 28%, showing AI costs or competition are eroding the core franchise, not just cash flow.
TTM ROIC falls below 12%, showing the capex build-out is diluting returns.
TTM FCF margin (cash-flow page, trailing) still below 10% after two further quarterly reports, i.e. the spend is not converting to cash.
Revenue growth stays below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters (income statement).

replacement_reason: The China/HK group is at the 25% cap and cash is near the 1.5% floor, so a China/HK holding must go. Tencent's ROIC of 16.5% beats the brewer's 11.9% and its WeChat network moat is wider, at a deeper discount to its own history; selling the largest China/HK weight frees enough room for Tencent at full size.
